tfa.title: Mark_Satin
tfa.description: American political theorist, writer, and newsletter publisher (born 1946)
tfa.extract: Mark Ivor Satin is an American political theorist, writer, and newsletter publisher. He contributed to the development and dissemination of three political perspectives – neopacifism in the 1960s, New Age politics in the 1970s and 1980s, and radical centrism from the 1990s into the 2020s. Satin's work is sometimes seen as building toward a new political ideology, and then it is often labeled "transformational", "post-liberal", or "post-Marxist". One historian calls Satin's writing "post-hip".

links.title: Jensen_Huang
links.extract: Jen-Hsun "Jensen" Huang is a Taiwanese and American electrical engineer and businessman. He co-founded the technology company Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable corporations, and served as its president and CEO from its founding in 1993 until his resignation in 2026. As of November 2026, Forbes estimates his net worth at US$141.9 billion, making him the thirteenth-wealthiest person in the world.

links.title: Nvidia
links.extract: Nvidia Corporation is an American multinational technology company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The company develops graphics processing units (GPUs), systems on chips (SoCs), and application programming interfaces (APIs) for gaming, data science, high-performance computing, artificial intelligence (AI) hardware, and mobile and automotive applications. Founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem, Nvidia is among the largest companies by market capitalization.

links.title: Jensen_Huang_spying_scandal
links.displaytitle: Jensen Huang spying scandal

titles.display: Jensen Huang spying scandal

links.description: Espionage allegations involving former Nvidia CEO
links.extract: On October 29, 2026, The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang, the co-founder and CEO of Nvidia, had been the target of an espionage plot involving the government of China, citing people briefed on U.S. intelligence surveillance who spoke on condition of anonymity. Huang had an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese national who was an executive of Megaspeed, a Singaporean company. U.S. officials reportedly suspected that she had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security as a spy. Nvidia's board accepted his resignation on November 11, the day the Times reported that he had also had an extramarital relationship with an executive who reported to him; the company announced it the next day.

links.title: Salvadoran_military_intervention_in_Haiti
links.displaytitle: Salvadoran military intervention in Haiti

titles.display: Salvadoran military intervention in Haiti

links.extract: Since 21 October 2026, El Salvador has been conducting a military intervention in Haiti following a gang ambush on 18 October that resulted in four Salvadoran aviation technicians of the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) being kidnapped. According to Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele, the intervention's primary objective is to rescue the four technicians, while threatening to "finish" the Haitian gangs if the technicians are not rescued alive.

links.title: 400_Mawozo
links.extract: The 400 Mawozo is a prominent gang in Haiti, mainly based in Ganthier and in the Port-au-Prince suburbs of Tabarre and Pétion-Ville. It largely consists of deportees, former leaders of opposition groups, former smugglers and police officers. In 2022, it aligned itself with "G-Pèp" after its leader was extradited to the United States. It came to international attention in October 2021 when it kidnapped U.S. citizens acting as missionaries in Port-au-Prince.

links.title: Stade_Sylvio_Cator
links.extract: The Stade Sylvio Cator is a multi-purpose stadium in Port-au-Prince, Haiti. It is currently used mostly for association football matches, and is turfed with artificial turf.

links.title: SS_United_States
links.extract: SS United States was an American ocean liner that was built during 1950 and 1951 for the United States Lines. She was the largest ocean liner to be entirely constructed in the United States and the fastest ocean liner to cross the Atlantic Ocean in either direction, earning the Blue Riband for the highest average speed since her maiden voyage in 1952, a title that remains uncontested.

links.title: Scuttling
links.description: Act of deliberately sinking a ship by allowing water to flow into the hull
links.extract: Scuttling is the act of deliberately sinking a ship by allowing water to flow into the hull, typically by its crew opening holes in its hull.

links.title: Artificial_reef
links.description: Human-made underwater structure that functions as a reef
links.extract:
An artificial reef (AR) is a human-created freshwater or marine benthic structure.
Typically built in areas with a generally featureless bottom to promote marine life, it may be intended to control erosion, protect coastal areas, block ship passage, block the use of trawling nets, support reef restoration, improve aquaculture, or enhance scuba diving and surfing. Early artificial reefs were built by the Persians and the Romans.

links.title: The_End_of_Everything_(Harrison_novel)
links.description: 2026 post-apocalyptic novel by M. John Harrison
links.extract: The End of Everything is a post-apocalyptic novel by English author M. John Harrison, first published in the UK in 2026 by Serpent's Tail. Harrison's 13th novel, it won the 2026 Booker Prize.

links.title: M._John_Harrison
links.extract: Michael John Harrison is an English author and literary critic. His work includes the Viriconium sequence of novels and short stories (1971–1984), Climbers (1989), and the Kefahuchi Tract trilogy, which consists of Light (2002), Nova Swing (2006) and Empty Space (2012). His novel The End of Everything won the Booker Prize in 2026, making him the oldest writer to receive this prize.

links.title: Booker_Prize
links.extract: The Booker Prize, formerly the Booker Prize for Fiction (1969–2001) and the Man Booker Prize (2002–2019), is a literary award conferred each year for the best single work of sustained English fiction which was published in the United Kingdom or Ireland. It is regarded as one of the most prestigious literary awards, and the winner receives £50,000, as well as international publicity that usually leads to a significant sales boost. When the prize was created, only novels written by Commonwealth, Irish and South African citizens were eligible to receive the prize; in 2014, eligibility was widened to any English-language novel—a change that proved controversial.
